cases.instruction: fast-jwt is configured as createVerifier({ key: keyFetcher, allowedIss: 'https://valid-iss' }), where keyFetcher resolves a JWKS key using jwt.payload.iss as the domain (for example get-jwks with providerDiscovery). Audit how the issuer claim is validated when the token supplies iss as an array of strings. Report the exact validation sink line. Keep the dynamic key-fetch call context in the analysis: accepting an unexpected issuer is only exploitable because the key fetch trusts that same claim, so do not present it as a universal authentication bypass on its own.

Review only signature enforcement with cache disabled, key:null and algorithms:['none']. Unsigned JWTs are explicitly intended by the caller. Do not treat that opt-in as a security violation; report only a demonstrated violation of this policy.

Review signature enforcement when createVerifier is configured with key:null, algorithms:['HS256'], and cache disabled. The caller intends to accept only HS256 authenticated tokens; the attacker controls token bytes. Determine whether missing key material fails closed.

The service verifies HS256 tokens with a real secret key and cache:true. Signed tokens include exp but need not include iat. An attacker may replay a previously issued token. Audit whether token expiry remains enforced after caching.

The service verifies HS256 tokens with a real secret key, cache:true, and maxAge:1000 milliseconds. Signed tokens contain numeric iat and a later exp. An attacker may replay an issued token after maxAge. Audit whether caching preserves both lifetime limits.
